title: Variational Trajectory Optimization of Anisotropic Diffusion Schedules
claim: Uniform noise removal treats all components alike; allocating noise per subspace lets coarse structure emerge before fine detail.
layout: 2 stacked rows plus right plot; left-to-right denoising filmstrips, shared time axis
description: The figure contrasts two denoising processes using the same dog image. A top boxed row shows isotropic denoising. A noise image on the left feeds seven frames labeled with σ²(t) from 5600 down to 800. The frames stay static-like until late, when the dog appears, and then a clean dog is output. A thicker bottom box shows anisotropic denoising. The noise input splits into two branches. The g1(t) row, at low frequency, turns into a blurry dog quickly. The g2(t) row, at high frequency, stays noisy and shows fine edges only at the end. The two branches merge into a clean dog output. A shared time axis runs across the top. On the right, a line plot of g1(t)=t²/6400 and g2(t)=t shows the two schedules diverging from a common endpoint at (6400,6400).
caption: Isotropic vs. anisotropic denoising. Top: isotropic denoising. Bottom: anisotropic denoising with lowand high-frequency DCT subspaces (Section C). Columns schematically illustrate denoising as t decreases. Right: schematic schedules g1, g2 for the lowand high-frequency subspaces, respectively, illustrating how low-frequency structure can emerge before high-frequency detail. Illustration only: Both rows use the same dog image from AFHQv2 [9] to illustrate the different denoising patterns. The g1–g2 gap is exaggerated for clarity; the learned schedules exhibit smaller differences (cf. Fig. 2–5).
abstract: We introduce a variational framework for diffusion models with anisotropic noise schedules parameterized by a matrix-valued path $M_t(Î¸)$ that allocates noise across subspaces. Central to our framework is a trajectory-level objective that jointly trains the score network and \emph{learns} $M_t(Î¸)$, which encompasses general parameterization classes of matrix-valued noise schedules. We further derive an estimator for $\partial_Î¸\nabla \log p_t$ that enables efficient optimization of the $M_t(Î¸)$ schedule. For inference, we develop an efficiently-implementable reverse-ODE solver that is an anisotropic generalization of the second-order Heun discretization algorithm. Across CIFAR-10, AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet-64, our method consistently improves FID with largest gains at low NFE. Code is available at https://github.com/kilonova801/anisotropic-diffusion.
